answer.rationale: The write-path latency climb began roughly 30 minutes after the release went out (2h ago vs. 90 min of climbing). Settlement writes are at daily peak, so the failing build is corrupting the most expensive path. memory_b1 shows a prior release-caused latency spike was fully resolved by rolling back to the known-good build, with no customer-facing impact. memory_b4 would confirm that circuit breakers could protect the checkout path if the root cause turns out to be an external dependency rather than the release itself, giving a fallback if the rollback does not restore p99. One intervention now: roll the release back. If the latency does not recover within the next monitoring window, escalate to circuit-breaker enablement.
